Can a 12B active parameter model run on a single B300 GPU and match a model four times its size?

Here are the latest developments in the AI space today.

📦 Thinking Machines Lab has released Inkling-Small, an open weights multimodal MoE model with 276B total and 12B active parameters. The NVFP4 checkpoint matches the performance of the original Inkling at a quarter of the size and runs on a single NVIDIA B300 GPU.

🔍 Onton has launched Ontology 1, a neurosymbolic search model for conversational, multimodal product search. In a 90-query benchmark scored by three independent LLM judges, it achieved a mean precision@10 of 0.630, outperforming Google Shopping at 0.543 and Amazon at 0.469.

📰 Reports indicate that OpenAI's super PAC is funding an AI-generated news site called Model Republic. The platform uses AI bots as reporters to publish articles that advance political agendas and target industry critics.

💬 Developer feedback is shifting for Anthropic as users report degradation in Opus 5 since the company began charging for Fable 5. Complaints include increased hallucinations, a defensive tone, and sudden account bans when trying to run Claude Code.

The rapid optimization of models like Inkling-Small shows how quickly hardware barriers are falling for local deployments. At the same time, the sudden shifts in proprietary model quality and platform access highlight the volatility of relying solely on closed APIs.

Which of these updates do you think will have the biggest impact on your current development workflow?
